what: Cosine similarity of speaker embeddings for pairs of real recordings: different utterances by the same person, and utterances by different people. Sets the thresholds of bolo.similarity (SAME_SPEAKER 0.50, SIMILAR 0.30) and the multi-speaker warning of bolo.voices (MULTI_SPEAKER_SIMILARITY 0.40).
embedding_model: pyannote-3.0-eres2net (3D-Speaker ERes2Net, VoxCeleb, run by sherpa-onnx 2.0.1)
data: LibriSpeech dev-clean (CC BY 4.0, https://www.openslr.org/12): the first 16 speakers of the archive, 5 utterances each between 4 and 15 s (80 clips, 16 kHz read speech)
hardware: 4 vCPU x86_64 (Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz), no GPU

window_consistency.what: Two utterances joined and cut into 3 s windows; the lowest similarity of a window to the mean of the others. One speaker: two utterances of the same person. Two speakers: one utterance each of two people.

caveats: Real read speech by native English speakers. Synthesised speech, other languages, telephone audio and noisy rooms were not part of this set; scores of cloned speech are compared with these real-pair numbers, which is a rule of thumb, not proof.
Another embedding model (voice_similarity_model) has another scale: the verdicts are only marked calibrated for this one.
16 speakers is a small set: the tails (min/max) are rough.
